### 6.5.4 Distributed Tracing

#### 6.5.4.1 AWS X-Ray Integration (Planned)

**Distributed Tracing Architecture:**

AWS X-Ray provides end-to-end request tracing across the distributed system, enabling identification of performance bottlenecks and failure points:

**X-Ray Instrumentation Points:**

- Flask API request handlers (entry point)
- MongoDB database queries (subsegments)
- Redis cache operations (subsegments)
- S3 API calls (subsegments)
- External LLM API requests (subsegments)
- Auth0 authentication calls (subsegments)

**Trace Visualization:**

```mermaid
graph LR
    ALB[ALB<br/>Trace Start<br/>10ms] --> Flask[Flask Handler<br/>1250ms total]
    Flask --> Auth{JWT Validation<br/>Redis<br/>2ms}
    Auth --> DB[MongoDB Query<br/>25ms]
    DB --> LLM[LLM API Call<br/>OpenAI<br/>1200ms]
    LLM --> Cache[Redis Cache Write<br/>3ms]
    Cache --> Response[Response Assembly<br/>20ms]
    Response --> ALBEnd[ALB<br/>Trace End]
    
    style ALB fill:#FF9900
    style Flask fill:#90EE90
    style LLM fill:#FFB6C1
    style DB fill:#4DB33D,color:#fff
    style Cache fill:#DC382D,color:#fff
```

#### 6.5.4.2 Trace Sampling Strategy

**Sampling Configuration:**

To balance trace coverage with cost, X-Ray implements intelligent sampling:

| Request Type | Sampling Rate | Rationale |
|-------------|---------------|-----------|
| **All Errors** | 100% | Complete error visibility |
| **Slow Requests (>2s)** | 100% | Performance investigation |
| **Successful Requests** | 5% | Representative sample |
| **Health Checks** | 0% | Reduce noise |

**Trace Retention:**

- **X-Ray Trace Storage**: 30 days
- **Trace Query Performance**: <5 seconds for 24-hour window
- **Service Map Generation**: Real-time (updated every 60 seconds)

### 6.5.5 Health Monitoring

#### 6.5.5.1 Multi-Layer Health Checks

**Health Check Hierarchy:**

The system implements health checks at four distinct layers ensuring comprehensive availability monitoring:

**1. Container Health Checks (Docker HEALTHCHECK):**

```
Protocol: HTTP
Endpoint: GET /health
Port: 8000
Interval: 30 seconds
Timeout: 5 seconds
Retries: 3 consecutive failures
Action: ECS terminates and replaces unhealthy container
```

**2. ALB Target Health Checks:**

```
Protocol: HTTP
Endpoint: GET /health
Port: 8000
Interval: 30 seconds
Timeout: 5 seconds
Healthy Threshold: 2 consecutive successes
Unhealthy Threshold: 3 consecutive failures
Deregistration Delay: 60 seconds
Action: ALB stops routing traffic to unhealthy target
```

**3. ECS Service Health Monitoring:**

- **Desired Task Count vs. Running Task Count**: Alert if running < desired for >5 minutes
- **Task Replacement Rate**: Track task churn rate (high churn indicates instability)
- **Health Check Failure Rate**: Percentage of targets failing health checks

**4. Application-Level Health Endpoint:**

The `/health` endpoint performs comprehensive dependency checks:

```json
{
  "status": "healthy",
  "timestamp": "2024-11-06T15:30:45.123Z",
  "version": "1.2.3",
  "uptime_seconds": 3600,
  "dependencies": {
    "mongodb": {
      "status": "healthy",
      "latency_ms": 12,
      "connection_pool_utilization": 45
    },
    "redis": {
      "status": "healthy",
      "latency_ms": 2,
      "memory_utilization_percent": 62
    },
    "auth0": {
      "status": "healthy",
      "last_check": "2024-11-06T15:30:40.000Z"
    }
  }
}
```

#### 6.5.5.2 Health Check Failure Response

**Automated Recovery Flow:**

```mermaid
graph TB
    Start([Health Check Executed]) --> CheckResult{Check<br/>Result?}
    
    CheckResult -->|Pass| Success[Update Last Success<br/>Timestamp]
    CheckResult -->|Fail| Increment[Increment<br/>Failure Counter]
    
    Success --> ResetCounter[Reset Failure Counter]
    ResetCounter --> End([Continue Monitoring])
    
    Increment --> ThresholdCheck{Consecutive Failures<br/>≥ Threshold?}
    
    ThresholdCheck -->|No| End
    ThresholdCheck -->|Yes| MarkUnhealthy[Mark Container<br/>Unhealthy]
    
    MarkUnhealthy --> ALBAction[ALB: Stop Routing<br/>Traffic to Target]
    ALBAction --> ECSAction[ECS: Terminate<br/>Unhealthy Task]
    
    ECSAction --> ProvisionNew[ECS: Launch<br/>Replacement Task]
    ProvisionNew --> StartupCheck[New Task<br/>Health Checks]
    
    StartupCheck --> RegistrationWait{2 Consecutive<br/>Successes?}
    
    RegistrationWait -->|No| StartupCheck
    RegistrationWait -->|Yes| Register[ALB: Register<br/>New Target]
    
    Register --> Alert[CloudWatch Alert:<br/>Task Replacement Event]
    Alert --> End
    
    style CheckResult fill:#FFE4B5
    style ThresholdCheck fill:#FFE4B5
    style MarkUnhealthy fill:#FFB6C1
    style Register fill:#90EE90
```

### 6.5.6 Alerting and Notification

#### 6.5.6.1 Alert Classification and Severity Levels

**Alert Severity Framework:**

| Severity | Definition | Response Time | Notification Channel | Escalation |
|----------|-----------|---------------|---------------------|------------|
| **Critical** | Service outage, data loss risk, security breach | <5 minutes | PagerDuty + Phone Call | Immediate |
| **Warning** | Degraded performance, approaching thresholds | <30 minutes | Slack #alerts channel | If unresolved in 2 hours |
| **Info** | Capacity changes, successful deployments | Review daily | Email digest | None |

#### 6.5.6.2 Alert Routing and Escalation

**Alert Flow Architecture:**

```mermaid
graph TB
    Metric[CloudWatch Metric<br/>Threshold Breach] --> Alarm[CloudWatch Alarm<br/>State: ALARM]
    
    Alarm --> SNS[Amazon SNS Topic<br/>Alert Router]
    
    SNS --> ClassifyIntent{Alert<br/>Severity?}
    
    ClassifyIntent -->|Critical| PagerDuty[PagerDuty<br/>Page On-Call Engineer]
    ClassifyIntent -->|Warning| Slack[Slack #alerts<br/>Team Notification]
    ClassifyIntent -->|Info| Email[Email<br/>Ops Team Digest]
    
    PagerDuty --> Acknowledged{Acknowledged<br/>Within 5 min?}
    
    Acknowledged -->|Yes| Resolve[Engineer Investigates<br/>and Resolves]
    Acknowledged -->|No| EscalateL2[Escalate to L2<br/>Secondary On-Call]
    
    EscalateL2 --> AckL2{Acknowledged<br/>Within 5 min?}
    
    AckL2 -->|Yes| Resolve
    AckL2 -->|No| EscalateManager[Escalate to<br/>Engineering Manager]
    
    EscalateManager --> Resolve
    
    Slack --> Review[Team Reviews<br/>Within 30 min]
    Email --> DailyReview[Daily Review<br/>Ops Team]
    
    Resolve --> PostMortem[Post-Incident<br/>Review]
    Review --> End([End])
    DailyReview --> End
    PostMortem --> End
    
    style Acknowledged fill:#FFE4B5
    style AckL2 fill:#FFE4B5
    style PagerDuty fill:#06AC38,color:#fff
    style Slack fill:#4A154B,color:#fff
    style PostMortem fill:#87CEEB
```

#### 6.5.6.3 Alert Threshold Configuration

**Critical Alerts (PagerDuty):**

| Alert Name | Metric | Threshold | Evaluation Period | Action |
|-----------|--------|-----------|-------------------|--------|
| **High Error Rate** | 5xx response count / total requests | >5% | 2 consecutive minutes | Page on-call |
| **Low Availability** | Healthy target count | <2 targets | 1 minute | Page on-call |
| **Database Primary Failure** | MongoDB replica set status | Primary unavailable | Immediate | Page on-call |
| **Cache Connection Failure** | Redis connection errors | >0 | 1 minute | Page on-call |

**Warning Alerts (Slack):**

| Alert Name | Metric | Threshold | Evaluation Period | Action |
|-----------|--------|-----------|-------------------|--------|
| **High API Latency** | API P99 response time | >2 seconds | 5 minutes | Slack notification |
| **Database Connection Pool** | MongoDB connections used | >90% of max | 5 minutes | Slack + auto-scale |
| **High CPU Utilization** | ECS task CPU | >80% | 10 minutes | Slack + auto-scale |
| **Authentication Failures** | Failed login count | >100/minute | 1 minute | Slack (security review) |

**Cost and Capacity Alerts:**

| Alert Name | Metric | Threshold | Evaluation Period | Action |
|-----------|--------|-----------|-------------------|--------|
| **LLM Cost Spike** | Hourly LLM API spend | >$100/hour | Immediate | Review usage patterns |
| **Storage Growth** | S3 bucket size | >80% of budget | Daily | Lifecycle policy review |
| **High Cache Eviction** | Redis eviction count | >1000/hour | 1 hour | Increase cache capacity |

### 6.5.8 Performance Monitoring

#### 6.5.8.1 Performance Targets and SLAs

**System Availability Target: 99.9% ("Three Nines")**

As documented in Section 5.4.5.2 (Cross-Cutting Concerns), the system targets 99.9% availability translating to:

- **Monthly Maximum Downtime**: 43.8 minutes
- **Weekly Maximum Downtime**: 10.1 minutes
- **Daily Maximum Downtime**: 1.4 minutes

**API Response Time Targets:**

| Operation Type | Target P50 | Target P95 | Target P99 | Maximum Acceptable |
|----------------|-----------|-----------|-----------|-------------------|
| **Simple GET APIs** | <50ms | <100ms | <200ms | 500ms |
| **Complex Queries** | <200ms | <500ms | <1000ms | 2000ms |
| **File Operations** | <100ms | <300ms | <500ms | 1000ms |
| **AI Queries** | <2s | <5s | <10s | 15s |

**Throughput Targets:**

- **Concurrent Users**: 1,000 initially, scale to 10,000
- **Requests Per Second**: 1,000 RPS initially, scale to 10,000 RPS
- **Database Operations**: 10,000 ops/second (MongoDB supports 100,000+)

#### 6.5.8.2 Synthetic Monitoring

**CloudWatch Synthetics Canaries:**

Scheduled synthetic monitors execute every 5 minutes from multiple geographic locations testing critical user journeys:

**Canary Test Scenarios:**

| Canary Name | Test Scenario | Success Criteria | Frequency |
|------------|---------------|------------------|-----------|
| **Homepage Load** | Load homepage and measure TTFB | <3s total load time | Every 5 minutes |
| **API Authentication** | Complete OAuth flow | Successful token issuance | Every 5 minutes |
| **AI Query Test** | Submit test AI query | Response within 10s | Every 15 minutes |
| **File Upload Test** | Upload small test file | Successful S3 upload | Every 15 minutes |

**Geographic Distribution:**

- **Primary Region (us-east-1)**: Virginia, USA
- **Secondary Region (us-west-2)**: Oregon, USA
- **International**: London (eu-west-2), Singapore (ap-southeast-1)

#### 6.5.8.3 Real User Monitoring (Planned)

**Frontend Performance Tracking:**

Planned integration of Real User Monitoring (RUM) SDK to capture actual user experience metrics:

**Core Web Vitals:**

- **First Contentful Paint (FCP)**: Time to first rendered content (<1.8s target)
- **Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)**: Time to largest content (<2.5s target)
- **Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)**: Visual stability score (<0.1 target)
- **First Input Delay (FID)**: Interactivity delay (<100ms target)

**User Experience Metrics:**

- Page load performance by route
- API call latency from user perspective
- JavaScript error rates and stack traces
- Feature usage analytics for product decisions

### 6.5.9 Incident Response Integration

#### 6.5.9.1 Alert Triage and Response Process

**Incident Lifecycle:**

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> AlertTriggered: CloudWatch Alarm
    
    AlertTriggered --> Acknowledged: Engineer acknowledges (PagerDuty)
    
    Acknowledged --> Investigation: Gather context
    
    Investigation --> RootCause: Identify root cause
    
    RootCause --> Mitigation: Apply fix or workaround
    
    Mitigation --> Verification: Verify issue resolved
    
    Verification --> Monitoring: Monitor for recurrence
    
    Monitoring --> Resolved: No recurrence after 1 hour
    
    Resolved --> PostMortem: Schedule post-mortem
    
    PostMortem --> [*]: Incident closed
    
    Investigation --> Escalation: Unable to resolve
    Escalation --> Investigation: Senior engineer engaged
    
    note right of Investigation
        Tools:
        - CloudWatch Dashboards
        - CloudWatch Logs Insights
        - X-Ray Service Map
        - ECS Console
        - MongoDB Atlas Metrics
    end note
    
    note right of PostMortem
        Deliverables:
        - Timeline of events
        - Root cause analysis
        - Action items
        - Prevention measures
    end note
```

#### 6.5.9.2 On-Call Rotation and Escalation

**On-Call Schedule:**

- **Primary On-Call (L1)**: Senior Software Engineer, 1-week rotation
- **Secondary On-Call (L2)**: Staff Engineer, backup coverage
- **Escalation Path**: Engineering Manager → VP Engineering

**Escalation Triggers:**

- Primary on-call unresponsive for 5 minutes (auto-escalate to L2)
- Incident unresolved after 30 minutes (manual escalate to L2)
- Data loss risk or security breach (immediate escalate to manager)

#### 6.5.9.3 Post-Incident Review Process

**Post-Mortem Template:**

```
# Incident Post-Mortem

**Incident ID**: INC-2024-11-06-001
**Date**: 2024-11-06
**Severity**: Critical
**Duration**: 25 minutes (14:30 - 14:55 UTC)
**Participants**: [List of attendees]

#### Summary
Brief description of incident and user impact.

#### Timeline
- **14:30 UTC**: Alert triggered (high error rate)
- **14:32 UTC**: On-call engineer acknowledged
- **14:35 UTC**: Root cause identified (database connection pool exhausted)
- **14:40 UTC**: Mitigation applied (increased connection pool size)
- **14:50 UTC**: System recovered, error rate normalized
- **14:55 UTC**: Incident resolved

#### Root Cause
Detailed analysis of underlying cause.

#### Impact
- **Users Affected**: ~500 users (5% of active users)
- **Availability**: 99.94% (below 99.9% SLA target)
- **Revenue Impact**: Estimated $X lost

#### Resolution
Steps taken to resolve the incident.

#### Action Items
1. [ ] Increase default connection pool size (Owner: @engineer, Due: 2024-11-13)
2. [ ] Add connection pool utilization alert (Owner: @sre, Due: 2024-11-08)
3. [ ] Update runbook with troubleshooting steps (Owner: @engineer, Due: 2024-11-10)

#### Lessons Learned
- What went well
- What could be improved
- Prevention measures
```

#### 6.5.10.3 Monitoring Technology Stack

**AWS Services:**
- **Amazon CloudWatch Metrics**: Time-series metrics storage and analysis
- **Amazon CloudWatch Logs**: Centralized log aggregation with 15-month retention
- **AWS CloudWatch Logs Insights**: SQL-like log query engine
- **AWS CloudWatch Alarms**: Threshold-based alerting engine
- **Amazon SNS**: Alert notification routing
- **AWS X-Ray**: Distributed tracing platform (planned implementation)
- **CloudWatch Synthetics**: Synthetic monitoring canaries

**Third-Party Integrations:**
- **MongoDB Atlas Metrics**: Database performance monitoring
- **Auth0 Logs**: Authentication event streaming
- **PagerDuty**: Critical alert escalation and on-call management
- **Slack**: Team collaboration and warning-level notifications

#### 6.5.10.4 Monitoring Best Practices Applied

- **Three Pillars of Observability**: Metrics, logs, and traces for comprehensive visibility
- **Multi-Layer Health Checks**: Container, ALB target, ECS service, and application-level health monitoring
- **Structured Logging**: JSON format with correlation IDs for distributed request tracing
- **Severity-Based Alerting**: Critical (PagerDuty), Warning (Slack), Info (Email) based on business impact
- **SLA-Driven Targets**: 99.9% availability, specific latency targets per operation type
- **Cost-Aware Monitoring**: LLM API cost tracking, infrastructure spend monitoring
- **Security Monitoring Integration**: Failed authentication tracking, audit log analysis
- **Proactive Monitoring**: Synthetic tests, capacity planning alerts, trend analysis

## 6.6 Testing Strategy

### 6.6.1 Testing Strategy Overview

#### 6.6.1.1 Testing Philosophy and Approach

The NewNov_6_1 system implements a **comprehensive multi-layer testing strategy** that ensures code quality, system reliability, and production readiness through automated testing at unit, integration, and end-to-end levels. As documented in Section 1.3 (System Overview), the system is currently in initialization phase with no implementation code; all testing specifications represent planned testing architecture to be implemented during the development phase.

**Strategic Testing Objectives:**

| Objective | Implementation | Success Criteria |
|-----------|----------------|------------------|
| **Quality Assurance** | Automated testing at every commit with 80% minimum code coverage | Zero critical bugs in production |
| **Fast Feedback** | CI/CD pipeline executes tests in <10 minutes | Developers receive test results before context switching |
| **Production Confidence** | Comprehensive integration and E2E tests in staging environment | 100% deployment success rate |
| **Regression Prevention** | Automated regression suite covering all critical user journeys | Zero regression bugs per release |

**Testing Pyramid Architecture:**

The testing strategy follows the testing pyramid pattern optimizing for fast, reliable feedback while minimizing test maintenance overhead:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Testing Pyramid"
        E2E[End-to-End Tests<br/>10% of test suite<br/>Synthetic Monitoring<br/>Critical User Journeys<br/>~50 tests]
        Integration[Integration Tests<br/>30% of test suite<br/>API Testing<br/>Database Integration<br/>External Service Mocking<br/>~150 tests]
        Unit[Unit Tests<br/>60% of test suite<br/>Function-Level Testing<br/>Component Testing<br/>Business Logic Validation<br/>~300 tests]
    end
    
    E2E --> Integration
    Integration --> Unit
    
    style E2E fill:#FFB6C1
    style Integration fill:#FFE4B5
    style Unit fill:#90EE90
```

**Testing Maturity Roadmap:**

| Phase | Timeline | Testing Capabilities | Coverage Target |
|-------|----------|---------------------|-----------------|
| **Phase 1: Foundation** | Launch (Month 0-3) | Unit tests, basic integration tests, manual E2E testing | 80% code coverage |
| **Phase 2: Automation** | Month 3-6 | Automated E2E tests, synthetic monitoring, performance testing | 85% code coverage |
| **Phase 3: Optimization** | Month 6-12 | Parallel test execution, flaky test management, visual regression testing | 90% code coverage |
| **Phase 4: Intelligence** | Year 2+ | AI-powered test generation, predictive test selection, chaos engineering | Maintain 90% coverage |

#### 6.6.1.2 Testing Scope and Boundaries

**In-Scope Testing:**

- Backend API endpoints (Flask REST API)
- Frontend components (React web, React Native mobile)
- Database operations (MongoDB queries, transactions)
- Authentication and authorization flows (Auth0 integration)
- External service integrations (LLM providers, S3, Redis)
- Security controls and compliance requirements
- Performance and scalability characteristics
- Cross-browser and cross-platform compatibility

**Out-of-Scope Testing:**

- Third-party managed service internals (Auth0, MongoDB Atlas, AWS services)
- Load testing beyond 10,000 concurrent users (reserved for performance engineering)
- Manual exploratory testing (delegated to QA team)
- Accessibility compliance testing (WCAG 2.1 AA - separate audit process)

**Mocking Strategy:**

Unit tests mock all external dependencies ensuring tests are fast, deterministic, and isolated:

```python
# Example: Mock external services in conftest.py
@pytest.fixture
def mock_mongodb(mocker):
    """Mock MongoDB database connection"""
    mock_db = mocker.patch('src.database.mongodb.get_db')
    mock_collection = mocker.MagicMock()
    mock_db.return_value = {'users': mock_collection}
    return mock_collection

@pytest.fixture
def mock_auth0(mocker):
    """Mock Auth0 JWT validation"""
    mock_validate = mocker.patch('src.auth.validate_jwt')
    mock_validate.return_value = {
        'user_id': 'test_user_123',
        'email': 'test@example.com',
        'roles': ['standard_user']
    }
    return mock_validate

@pytest.fixture
def mock_llm_api(mocker):
    """Mock LLM API calls to avoid costs"""
    mock_llm = mocker.patch('src.services.llm_service.LLMService.query')
    mock_llm.return_value = {
        'response': 'Mock LLM response',
        'tokens_used': 150,
        'cost': 0.003
    }
    return mock_llm
```

**Test Naming Conventions:**

Tests follow the `test_<function>_<scenario>_<expected_result>` naming pattern ensuring clarity and self-documentation:

```python
# Good test names (clear and descriptive)
def test_create_user_with_valid_data_returns_201():
    """Test user creation with valid input returns 201 Created"""
    pass

def test_create_user_with_duplicate_email_returns_409():
    """Test user creation with duplicate email returns 409 Conflict"""
    pass

def test_authenticate_user_with_invalid_password_returns_401():
    """Test authentication with incorrect password returns 401 Unauthorized"""
    pass

#### Bad test names (avoid)
def test_user():  # Too vague
    pass

def test_1():  # No context
    pass
```

**Code Coverage Requirements:**

As documented in Section 3.7.4.1 (CI/CD Pipeline), the system enforces **80% minimum code coverage** across all modules with stricter requirements for critical code paths:

| Module Type | Coverage Requirement | Rationale |
|-------------|---------------------|-----------|
| **Security Code** | 95% minimum | Authentication, authorization, data encryption |
| **Business Logic** | 90% minimum | Core features, data transformations |
| **API Routes** | 85% minimum | HTTP endpoints, request validation |
| **Utility Functions** | 80% minimum | Helper functions, formatters |

**Pytest Configuration:**

```ini
# pytest.ini
[pytest]
testpaths = tests/unit tests/integration
python_files = test_*.py
python_classes = Test*
python_functions = test_*

addopts = 
    --verbose
    --cov=src
    --cov-report=html:coverage_html
    --cov-report=term-missing
    --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml
    --cov-fail-under=80
    --strict-markers
    --tb=short
    -ra
    --maxfail=5

markers =
    unit: Unit tests (fast, isolated)
    integration: Integration tests (require external dependencies)
    slow: Tests that take >1 second
    security: Security-critical tests
    smoke: Smoke tests for rapid validation

[coverage:run]
omit =
    tests/*
    */migrations/*
    */venv/*
    */virtualenv/*

[coverage:report]
exclude_lines =
    pragma: no cover
    def __repr__
    raise AssertionError
    raise NotImplementedError
    if __name__ == .__main__.:
    if TYPE_CHECKING:
```

**Component Testing Strategy:**

React components tested using React Testing Library emphasizing user-centric testing:

```typescript
// Example: Component test with user interactions
import { render, screen, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { LoginForm } from './LoginForm';

describe('LoginForm', () => {
  test('submits credentials when form is valid', async () => {
    const mockOnSubmit = jest.fn();
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    
    render(<LoginForm onSubmit={mockOnSubmit} />);
    
    // Simulate user interactions
    await user.type(screen.getByLabelText(/email/i), 'test@example.com');
    await user.type(screen.getByLabelText(/password/i), 'SecurePass123!');
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: /login/i }));
    
    await waitFor(() => {
      expect(mockOnSubmit).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
        email: 'test@example.com',
        password: 'SecurePass123!'
      });
    });
  });
  
  test('displays validation error when email is invalid', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    
    render(<LoginForm onSubmit={jest.fn()} />);
    
    await user.type(screen.getByLabelText(/email/i), 'invalid-email');
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: /login/i }));
    
    expect(screen.getByText(/invalid email address/i)).toBeInTheDocument();
```
```typescript
  });
});
```

**Database Integration Testing:**

As documented in Section 6.2 (Database Design), integration tests validate MongoDB operations with actual database connections:

```python
# Example: MongoDB integration test
@pytest.mark.integration
class TestUserRepository:
    """Integration tests for user data access layer"""
    
    @pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
    def setup_test_db(self, mongodb_test_connection):
        """Setup test database before each test"""
        self.db = mongodb_test_connection
        self.users_collection = self.db['users']
        yield
        # Cleanup: Drop test collection after test
        self.users_collection.delete_many({})
    
    def test_create_user_persists_to_database(self):
        """Test user creation writes to MongoDB"""
        user_data = {
            'email': 'test@example.com',
            'full_name': 'Test User',
            'role': 'standard_user'
        }
        
        # Execute: Create user
        result = self.users_collection.insert_one(user_data)
        user_id = result.inserted_id
        
        # Verify: User exists in database
        retrieved_user = self.users_collection.find_one({'_id': user_id})
        assert retrieved_user is not None
        assert retrieved_user['email'] == 'test@example.com'
        assert retrieved_user['role'] == 'standard_user'
    
    def test_find_user_by_email_returns_correct_document(self):
        """Test user lookup by email"""
        # Setup: Insert test user
        self.users_collection.insert_one({
            'email': 'existing@example.com',
            'full_name': 'Existing User',
            'role': 'power_user'
        })
        
        # Execute: Find by email
        found_user = self.users_collection.find_one({'email': 'existing@example.com'})
        
        # Verify: Correct user returned
        assert found_user is not None
        assert found_user['role'] == 'power_user'
```

**Redis Cache Integration Testing:**

```python
@pytest.mark.integration
class TestCacheService:
    """Integration tests for Redis cache operations"""
    
    @pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
    def setup_redis(self, redis_test_connection):
        """Setup Redis test connection"""
        self.redis = redis_test_connection
        yield
        # Cleanup: Flush test Redis DB
        self.redis.flushdb()
    
    def test_cache_set_and_get_returns_stored_value(self):
        """Test basic cache set/get operations"""
        key = 'test_key'
        value = '{"user_id": "123", "email": "test@example.com"}'
        
        # Execute: Cache set
        self.redis.setex(key, 300, value)  # 5-minute TTL
        
        # Verify: Cache get retrieves value
        cached_value = self.redis.get(key)
        assert cached_value.decode('utf-8') == value
    
    def test_cache_expiration_removes_key_after_ttl(self):
        """Test cache key expires after TTL"""
        key = 'expiring_key'
        value = 'test_value'
        
        # Execute: Set with 1-second TTL
        self.redis.setex(key, 1, value)
        
        # Verify: Key exists immediately
        assert self.redis.exists(key) == 1
        
        # Wait for expiration
        time.sleep(2)
        
        # Verify: Key expired
        assert self.redis.exists(key) == 0
```

```python
    def test_get_user_profile_returns_authenticated_user_data(self, api_client, auth_token):
        """Test GET /api/users/me returns current user profile"""
        # Execute: Request user profile with valid JWT
        response = api_client.get(
            '/api/users/me',
            headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {auth_token}'}
        )
        
        # Verify: Response successful with user data
        assert response.status_code == 200
        data = response.json()
        assert 'user_id' in data
        assert 'email' in data
        assert 'role' in data
    
    def test_update_user_profile_persists_changes(self, api_client, auth_token):
        """Test PATCH /api/users/me updates user profile"""
        update_data = {'full_name': 'Updated Name'}
        
        # Execute: Update profile
        response = api_client.patch(
            '/api/users/me',
            json=update_data,
            headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {auth_token}'}
        )
        
        # Verify: Update successful
        assert response.status_code == 200
        
        # Verify: Changes persisted in database
        profile_response = api_client.get(
            '/api/users/me',
            headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {auth_token}'}
        )
        assert profile_response.json()['full_name'] == 'Updated Name'
    
    def test_access_other_user_profile_returns_403(self, api_client, auth_token):
        """Test users cannot access other users' profiles"""
        other_user_id = 'different_user_456'
        
        # Execute: Attempt to access another user's profile
        response = api_client.get(
            f'/api/users/{other_user_id}',
            headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {auth_token}'}
        )
        
        # Verify: Access denied
        assert response.status_code == 403
        assert response.json()['error'] == 'INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS'
```

#### 6.6.3.3 External Service Mocking

**LLM API Mocking Strategy:**

To avoid costs and ensure deterministic tests, LLM API calls are mocked in integration tests:

```python

@pytest.mark.integration
```

### 6.6.4 End-to-End Testing Strategy

#### 6.6.4.1 E2E Test Scenarios

**Critical User Journey Coverage:**

End-to-end tests validate complete user workflows across frontend and backend systems:

| User Journey | Test Scenario | Success Criteria |
|--------------|---------------|------------------|
| **User Registration** | Complete signup flow from registration form to email verification | User account created, verification email sent, login successful |
| **Authentication** | Login with valid credentials, access protected resources | JWT token issued, API requests authorized |
| **AI Interaction** | Submit AI query, receive response, view conversation history | AI response returned within 10s, conversation persisted |
| **File Management** | Upload file to S3, download file, delete file | File uploaded successfully, download works, deletion confirmed |

**E2E Test Implementation:**

E2E tests leverage CloudWatch Synthetics for production monitoring and Playwright for development testing:

```typescript
// Example: Playwright E2E test
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('User Authentication Flow', () => {
  test('user can login with valid credentials', async ({ page }) => {
    // Navigate to login page
    await page.goto('https://app.newnov6.com/login');
    
    // Fill login form
    await page.fill('input[name="email"]', 'test@example.com');
    await page.fill('input[name="password"]', 'SecurePass123!');
    
    // Submit form
    await page.click('button[type="submit"]');
    
    // Verify: Redirected to dashboard
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/.*dashboard/);
    
    // Verify: User profile displayed
    await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="user-profile"]')).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="user-email"]')).toContainText('test@example.com');
  });
  
  test('user cannot login with invalid credentials', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('https://app.newnov6.com/login');
    
    await page.fill('input[name="email"]', 'test@example.com');
    await page.fill('input[name="password"]', 'WrongPassword');
    await page.click('button[type="submit"]');
    
    // Verify: Error message displayed
    await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="error-message"]')).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="error-message"]')).toContainText('Invalid credentials');
  });
});
```

#### 6.6.4.2 Synthetic Monitoring

**CloudWatch Synthetics Canaries:**

As documented in Section 6.5.8.2 (Monitoring - Synthetic Monitoring), production E2E testing runs continuously via CloudWatch Synthetics:

| Canary Name | Test Scenario | Frequency | Timeout | Alerting |
|-------------|---------------|-----------|---------|----------|
| **Homepage Load Test** | Load homepage, measure TTFB and total load time | Every 5 minutes | 30 seconds | <3s load time |
| **API Health Check** | Call /health endpoint, verify dependencies | Every 5 minutes | 10 seconds | All dependencies healthy |
| **Authentication Flow** | Complete OAuth flow, obtain JWT token | Every 5 minutes | 60 seconds | Token issued successfully |
| **AI Query Test** | Submit test query, verify response | Every 15 minutes | 30 seconds | Response within 10s |
| **File Upload Test** | Upload test file to S3, verify success | Every 15 minutes | 30 seconds | Upload successful |

**Canary Failure Alerting:**

Synthetic test failures trigger CloudWatch alarms escalating to PagerDuty for immediate investigation:

```
Severity: CRITICAL
Alert: Synthetic canary failure detected
Threshold: 2 consecutive failures
Action: Page on-call engineer via PagerDuty
Escalation: L2 on-call if unacknowledged after 5 minutes
```

#### 6.6.4.4 Performance Testing

**Load Testing Strategy:**

As documented in Section 5.4.5 (Cross-Cutting Concerns - Performance), the system targets specific performance thresholds:

**Performance Test Scenarios:**

| Test Type | Target Metrics | Tools | Frequency |
|-----------|----------------|-------|-----------|
| **Load Testing** | 1,000 concurrent users, 1,000 RPS sustained | Locust or k6 | Weekly (staging) |
| **Stress Testing** | 10,000 concurrent users, identify breaking point | Locust or k6 | Monthly (staging) |
| **Spike Testing** | Sudden traffic spike (1,000 → 5,000 users in 1 min) | Locust or k6 | Monthly (staging) |
| **Endurance Testing** | Sustained load for 24 hours, identify memory leaks | Locust or k6 | Quarterly (staging) |

**Response Time Thresholds:**

| Operation Type | P50 Target | P95 Target | P99 Target | Max Acceptable |
|----------------|-----------|-----------|-----------|----------------|
| **Simple GET APIs** | <50ms | <100ms | <200ms | 500ms |
| **Complex Queries** | <200ms | <500ms | <1000ms | 2000ms |
| **File Operations** | <100ms | <300ms | <500ms | 1000ms |
| **AI Queries** | <2s | <5s | <10s | 15s |

**Load Test Execution Flow:**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant CI as CI/CD Pipeline
    participant Staging as Staging Environment
    participant Locust as Locust Load Generator
    participant CW as CloudWatch Metrics
    participant Alert as Alerting System
    
    CI->>Staging: Deploy to Staging
    Staging->>CI: Deployment Successful
    
    CI->>Locust: Trigger Load Test
    Locust->>Staging: Ramp up to 1,000 users
    Staging->>CW: Emit metrics (latency, errors)
    
    loop Performance Monitoring
        CW->>CW: Evaluate metrics vs. thresholds
    end
    
    Locust->>Staging: Sustained load for 10 minutes
    Staging->>CW: Continue metrics emission
    
    Locust->>CI: Test Complete
    CW->>CI: Export performance report
    
    alt Performance Degradation Detected
        CW->>Alert: Threshold breach
        Alert->>CI: Fail pipeline
        CI->>CI: Block deployment
    else Performance Acceptable
        CI->>CI: Pass quality gate
        CI->>CI: Proceed to production
    end
```

### 6.6.5 Test Automation Framework

#### 6.6.5.1 CI/CD Test Integration

**GitHub Actions Testing Workflow:**

As documented in Section 3.7.4 (CI/CD Pipeline), automated testing executes at multiple stages:

```mermaid
graph LR
    Push[Code Push/PR] --> Trigger{Branch?}
    
    Trigger -->|Feature Branch| FeatureCI[Feature CI]
    Trigger -->|Main Branch| MainCI[Main CI]
    Trigger -->|Staging Branch| StagingCI[Staging CI]
    Trigger -->|Production Tag| ProdCI[Production CI]
    
    FeatureCI --> Lint[Lint & Format Check]
    MainCI --> Lint
    StagingCI --> Lint
    ProdCI --> Lint
    
    Lint --> UnitTests[Unit Tests<br/>80% Coverage]
    
    UnitTests --> SecurityScan[Security Scan<br/>bandit, npm audit]
    
    SecurityScan --> Build[Build Docker Images]
    
    Build --> IntegrationDecision{Integration<br/>Tests?}
    
    IntegrationDecision -->|Feature/Main| SkipIntegration[Skip Integration Tests]
    IntegrationDecision -->|Staging/Prod| RunIntegration[Integration Tests<br/>Staging Environment]
    
    SkipIntegration --> Complete[Tests Complete]
    
    RunIntegration --> E2EDecision{E2E Tests?}
    
    E2EDecision -->|Staging| RunE2E[E2E Tests<br/>Playwright]
    E2EDecision -->|Production| SkipE2E[Skip E2E<br/>Use Synthetics]
    
    RunE2E --> PerformanceTest[Performance Tests<br/>Load Testing]
    SkipE2E --> Complete
    
    PerformanceTest --> QualityGate{Quality<br/>Gate Pass?}
    
    QualityGate -->|Pass| Complete
    QualityGate -->|Fail| BlockDeploy[Block Deployment<br/>Alert Team]
    
    Complete --> Success[Pipeline Success<br/>Proceed to Deployment]
    BlockDeploy --> Failure[Pipeline Failure<br/>Investigate]
    
    style UnitTests fill:#90EE90
    style IntegrationDecision fill:#FFE4B5
    style QualityGate fill:#FFE4B5
    style Success fill:#90EE90
    style Failure fill:#FFB6C1
```

**CI/CD Workflow Configuration:**

```yaml
# .github/workflows/backend-ci.yml
name: Backend CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop, staging]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    services:
      mongodb:
        image: mongo:7.0
        ports:
          - 27017:27017
      redis:
        image: redis:7.2
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
    
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          pip install -r requirements.txt
          pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
      
      - name: Lint with black and flake8
        run: |
          black --check src/ tests/
          flake8 src/ tests/ --max-line-length=100
      
      - name: Type check with mypy
        run: mypy src/
      
      - name: Run unit tests with coverage
        run: |
          pytest tests/unit/ \
            --cov=src \
            --cov-report=xml \
            --cov-report=term-missing \
            --cov-fail-under=80
      
      - name: Security scan with bandit
        run: bandit -r src/ -f json -o bandit-report.json
      
      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v3
        with:
          files: ./coverage.xml
          flags: unittests
      
      - name: Run integration tests (staging/production only)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/staging' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        run: pytest tests/integration/ --maxfail=5
```

#### 6.6.5.4 Flaky Test Management

**Flaky Test Detection:**

Automated detection of intermittent test failures indicating flakiness:

```python
# pytest plugin for flaky test detection
# conftest.py
def pytest_runtest_makereport(item, call):
    """Track test results for flakiness detection"""
    if call.when == "call":
        test_name = item.nodeid
        result = call.excinfo is None  # True = passed, False = failed
        
        # Record test result to database
        record_test_result(test_name, result)
        
        # Check flakiness: >5% failure rate over last 100 runs
        failure_rate = get_test_failure_rate(test_name, runs=100)
        if 0.05 < failure_rate < 0.95:
            # Flaky test detected (not always passing or failing)
            mark_test_flaky(test_name)
            send_slack_notification(f"Flaky test detected: {test_name}")
```

**Flaky Test Quarantine:**

Consistently flaky tests isolated to prevent blocking CI pipeline:

```python
# Mark flaky tests for quarantine
@pytest.mark.flaky(reruns=3, reruns_delay=2)
def test_sometimes_fails_due_to_timing():
    """Flaky test will retry up to 3 times"""
    pass

@pytest.mark.quarantine
def test_consistently_flaky_quarantined():
    """Quarantined test runs separately, doesn't block CI"""
    pass
```

**Flaky Test Remediation Process:**

```mermaid
graph TB
    Detect[Flaky Test Detected<br/>Failure Rate: 5-95%] --> Notify[Slack Notification<br/>Engineering Team]
    
    Notify --> Triage{Severity?}
    
    Triage -->|Critical Path| HighPriority[High Priority<br/>Fix Within 1 Sprint]
    Triage -->|Non-Critical| LowPriority[Low Priority<br/>Fix When Possible]
    
    HighPriority --> Investigate[Investigate Root Cause]
    LowPriority --> Quarantine[Quarantine Test<br/>Run Separately]
    
    Investigate --> RootCause{Root Cause?}
    
    RootCause -->|Timing Issue| AddRetries[Add Retries + Delays]
    RootCause -->|Test Data| IsolateData[Isolate Test Data]
    RootCause -->|External Dependency| MockDependency[Mock External Service]
    RootCause -->|Infrastructure| FixInfra[Fix Test Infrastructure]
    
    AddRetries --> Validate[Validate Fix<br/>Monitor 100 Runs]
    IsolateData --> Validate
    MockDependency --> Validate
    FixInfra --> Validate
    
    Validate --> Success{Stable?}
    
    Success -->|Yes| Restore[Restore to Main Suite]
    Success -->|No| Quarantine
    
    Quarantine --> Backlog[Add to Engineering Backlog]
    
    style Detect fill:#FFB6C1
    style Triage fill:#FFE4B5
    style Success fill:#FFE4B5
    style Restore fill:#90EE90
```

### 6.6.6 Quality Metrics and Gates

#### 6.6.6.1 Code Coverage Targets

**Coverage Requirements by Environment:**

As documented in Section 3.7.4.1 (CI/CD Pipeline), the system enforces minimum 80% code coverage with strict enforcement:

| Module Category | Coverage Target | Enforcement | Rationale |
|-----------------|----------------|-------------|-----------|
| **Security Modules** | 95% minimum | CI pipeline blocks <95% | Critical for authentication, authorization, encryption |
| **Business Logic** | 90% minimum | CI pipeline blocks <90% | Core features, data transformations, AI orchestration |
| **API Endpoints** | 85% minimum | CI pipeline blocks <85% | HTTP routes, request validation, response formatting |
| **Utility Functions** | 80% minimum | CI pipeline blocks <80% | Helper functions, formatters, validators |
| **UI Components** | 80% minimum | CI pipeline blocks <80% | React components, user interactions |

**Coverage Trend Monitoring:**

Track coverage trends over time identifying coverage improvements or regressions:

#### 6.6.6.4 Performance Test Thresholds

**API Performance Thresholds:**

As documented in Section 5.4.5 (Cross-Cutting Concerns - Performance), performance tests enforce specific latency targets:

| Metric | Measurement | Target | Warning Threshold | Critical Threshold |
|--------|-------------|--------|-------------------|-------------------|
| **API P50 Latency** | Median response time | <50ms | >75ms | >100ms |
| **API P95 Latency** | 95th percentile | <100ms | >150ms | >200ms |
| **API P99 Latency** | 99th percentile | <200ms | >400ms | >500ms |
| **Error Rate** | 5xx errors / total requests | <0.1% | >0.5% | >1% |
| **Throughput** | Requests per second | ≥1,000 RPS | <900 RPS | <800 RPS |

### 6.6.7 Security Testing

#### 6.6.7.1 Automated Security Scanning

**CI/CD Security Checks:**

As documented in Section 3.7.4.1 (CI/CD Pipeline), automated security scans execute on every build:

| Scanner | Target | Scan Frequency | Blocking Threshold |
|---------|--------|----------------|-------------------|
| **bandit** | Python source code | Every commit | Critical or High severity |
| **npm audit** | JavaScript dependencies | Every commit | Critical vulnerabilities |
| **Trivy** | Docker images | Every build | Critical CVEs |
| **OWASP Dependency Check** | All dependencies | Weekly | Known vulnerabilities |

**Security Scan Example:**

```yaml
# .github/workflows/security-scan.yml
name: Security Scan

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 2 * * 1'  # Weekly Monday 2 AM

jobs:
  security-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Run bandit security scan
        run: |
          pip install bandit
          bandit -r src/ -f json -o bandit-report.json
          bandit -r src/ -ll  # Fail on medium or higher
      
      - name: Run npm audit
        run: |
          cd frontend/
          npm audit --audit-level=critical
      
      - name: Scan Docker images with Trivy
        run: |
          docker build -t app:test .
          trivy image --severity CRITICAL,HIGH --exit-code 1 app:test
      
      - name: Upload security reports
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: security-reports
          path: |
            bandit-report.json
            npm-audit.json
            trivy-report.json
```

#### 6.6.7.2 Security Control Testing

**Authentication and Authorization Testing:**

As documented in Section 6.4 (Security Architecture), comprehensive security control testing validates authentication and authorization mechanisms:

| Control ID | Test Scenario | Expected Result | Test Frequency |
|-----------|---------------|-----------------|----------------|
| **AUTH-001** | MFA enrollment and validation | MFA required for admin users | Monthly |
| **AUTH-002** | Password complexity enforcement | Weak passwords rejected | Monthly |
| **AUTH-003** | Breached password detection | Breached passwords blocked | Monthly |
| **AUTH-004** | Account lockout after failures | Account locked after 10 attempts | Monthly |
| **AUTH-005** | JWT token expiration | Expired tokens rejected | Monthly |
| **AUTH-006** | JWT signature validation | Invalid signatures rejected | Continuous |
| **AUTH-007** | Token revocation | Revoked tokens blocked | Monthly |
| **AUTH-008** | Session management | httpOnly cookies, Secure flag | Quarterly |

**Authorization Control Testing:**

| Control ID | Test Scenario | Expected Result | Test Frequency |
|-----------|---------------|-----------------|----------------|
| **AUTHZ-001** | RBAC permission enforcement | Users can only access permitted resources | Quarterly |
| **AUTHZ-002** | Resource ownership validation | Users can only access own resources | Quarterly |
| **AUTHZ-003** | Admin privilege verification | Admin bypass works correctly | Monthly |
| **AUTHZ-004** | Permission inheritance | Roles inherit correct permissions | Quarterly |

**Data Protection Testing:**

| Control ID | Test Scenario | Expected Result | Test Frequency |
|-----------|---------------|-----------------|----------------|
| **DATA-001** | Encryption at rest | All data encrypted in MongoDB, S3, Redis | Quarterly |
| **DATA-002** | Encryption in transit | All connections use TLS 1.2+ | Monthly |
| **DATA-003** | Key rotation | AWS KMS keys rotate annually | Annually |
| **DATA-004** | Secrets management | No secrets in code or logs | Quarterly |
| **DATA-005** | Data masking | PII scrubbed from logs | Monthly |
| **DATA-006** | GDPR erasure | Complete data deletion works | Quarterly |
| **DATA-007** | Data minimization | Only necessary data collected | Annually |
| **DATA-008** | Audit logging | All critical actions logged | Monthly |

#### 6.6.7.3 Compliance Testing

**GDPR Compliance Validation:**

As documented in Section 6.4.4.5 (Security Architecture - Compliance), GDPR compliance tested quarterly:

```python
@pytest.mark.compliance
class TestGDPRCompliance:
    """Test GDPR data subject rights implementation"""
    
    def test_right_to_access_exports_all_user_data(self, api_client, auth_token):
        """Test GDPR Article 15: Right to Access"""
        response = api_client.get(
            '/api/users/me/export',
            headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {auth_token}'}
        )
        
        assert response.status_code == 200
        data = response.json()
        
        # Verify all user data included
        assert 'profile' in data
        assert 'conversations' in data
        assert 'files' in data
        assert 'audit_logs' in data
    
    def test_right_to_erasure_deletes_all_user_data(self, api_client, auth_token, mongodb):
        """Test GDPR Article 17: Right to Erasure"""
        user_id = extract_user_id(auth_token)
        
        # Execute: Request account deletion
        response = api_client.delete(
            '/api/users/me',
            headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {auth_token}'}
        )
        
        assert response.status_code == 204
        
        # Verify: User data deleted from all collections
        assert mongodb['users'].find_one({'user_id': user_id}) is None
        assert mongodb['conversations'].count_documents({'user_id': user_id}) == 0
        assert mongodb['files'].count_documents({'user_id': user_id}) == 0
        
        # Verify: GDPR deletion logged
        deletion_log = mongodb['gdpr_deletions'].find_one({'user_id': user_id})
        assert deletion_log is not None
        assert deletion_log['deletion_timestamp'] is not None
```

#### 6.6.8.2 Test Data Flow

**Test Data Lifecycle:**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Dev as Developer
    participant Seed as Seed Scripts
    participant TestDB as Test Database
    participant Tests as Test Execution
    participant Cleanup as Cleanup Process
    
    Dev->>Seed: Run seed script
    Seed->>TestDB: Insert test data
    Note over TestDB: Test data:<br/>- Users<br/>- Conversations<br/>- Files
    
    Dev->>Tests: Execute test suite
    Tests->>TestDB: Query test data
    TestDB->>Tests: Return test data
    
    Tests->>TestDB: Create/modify data
    Note over TestDB: Test-specific data created
    
    Tests->>Tests: Assertions pass/fail
    
    Tests->>Cleanup: Test complete
    Cleanup->>TestDB: Delete test-created data
    Cleanup->>TestDB: Reset seed data
    
    Note over TestDB: Ready for next test run
```

```python
# tests/fixtures/seed_data.py
def seed_test_database(mongodb_connection):
    """Seed test database with predictable test data"""
    users_collection = mongodb_connection['users']

    test_users = [
        {
            'user_id': 'test_standard_user',
```

#### 6.6.10.4 Testing Best Practices Applied

- **Testing Pyramid**: 60% unit tests, 30% integration tests, 10% E2E tests optimizing for fast feedback
- **Test Isolation**: Mock external dependencies in unit tests, use dedicated test databases for integration tests
- **Deterministic Tests**: Fixed test data, mocked external services, controlled time/randomness
- **Fast Feedback**: Parallel test execution, fail-fast on critical failures, <10 minute CI pipeline
- **Comprehensive Coverage**: 80% minimum code coverage with higher requirements for security-critical code
- **Continuous Testing**: Automated testing on every commit, staging deployment, and production monitoring
- **Security-First Testing**: Automated security scans, compliance testing, security control validation
- **Performance Validation**: Load testing, response time thresholds, synthetic monitoring
- **Test Maintainability**: Clear naming conventions, test organization mirroring source code, shared fixtures
- **Quality Gates**: Multi-stage quality gates blocking deployment on test failures

#### 6.6.10.5 Key Testing Decisions

All testing architecture decisions referenced in this section:

1. **pytest as Backend Framework**: Industry-standard Python testing framework with rich plugin ecosystem
2. **Jest as Frontend Framework**: React-native testing framework with excellent TypeScript support
3. **80% Code Coverage Minimum**: Enforced in CI/CD pipeline balancing quality with development velocity
4. **Mocked External Services**: LLM APIs, Auth0, S3 mocked in unit/integration tests to reduce costs and ensure determinism
5. **CloudWatch Synthetics for Production E2E**: AWS-native synthetic monitoring running critical user journeys every 5 minutes
6. **Multi-Stage Quality Gates**: Progressive quality gates from unit tests through production deployment
7. **Parallel Test Execution**: pytest-xdist and Jest parallelization reducing CI pipeline time
8. **Security Testing in CI/CD**: Automated security scanning (bandit, npm audit, Trivy) on every build
9. **Test Environment Isolation**: Separate test databases and services preventing test interference
10. **Performance Testing in Staging**: Load testing executed in staging environment before production deployment

# 7. User Interface Design

## 7.1 UI Architecture Overview

### 7.1.1 Multi-Platform Strategy

The NewNov_6_1 system implements an ambitious **multi-platform user interface strategy** spanning six distinct presentation layer implementations. This architecture supports a phased rollout approach while maximizing code reuse and maintaining platform-native user experiences where appropriate.

**Supported Platforms:**

1. **React Web Application** - Primary platform, browser-based access
2. **React Native Mobile Application** - Cross-platform iOS and Android
3. **Native iOS Application** - Swift-based, platform-optimized
4. **Native Android Application** - Kotlin-based, Material Design 3
5. **Electron Desktop Application** - Cross-platform Windows, macOS, Linux
6. **Native macOS Application** - Objective-C with AppKit framework

The architecture prioritizes a **web-first development approach**, with mobile and desktop platforms following in subsequent phases. This strategy allows for rapid validation of core functionality while building toward comprehensive platform coverage.

### 7.1.2 Development Status

**Current Implementation Status:** The repository is in its initialization phase with no source code implementation present. The UI design documented in this section represents the **planned architecture** based on comprehensive technical specifications. All UI components, screens, and interaction patterns described herein constitute the design blueprint that will guide implementation.

**Repository Evidence:**
- Single file present: `README.md` (containing only "# NewNov_6_1")
- No source code directories established
- No UI component implementations
- No configuration files for frontend frameworks

This documentation serves as the authoritative reference for UI implementation teams across all platform development efforts.

### 7.1.3 Code Reuse Strategy

The system architecture achieves **70-80% code reuse** between React Web and React Native implementations through strategic architectural decisions:

**Shared Components:**
- TypeScript type definitions and interfaces
- API client logic and authentication handlers
- State management patterns (Zustand/Redux stores)
- Business logic and validation rules
- Utility functions and helper modules

**Platform-Specific Components:**
- Navigation implementations (react-router-dom vs React Navigation)
- File system interactions
- Platform-native UI components (buttons, inputs, modals)
- Gesture handlers and touch interactions
- Platform-specific APIs (camera, location, notifications)

**Desktop Code Reuse:**
The Electron desktop application leverages the React Web implementation directly, adding only platform-specific features such as native menus, system tray integration, and file system access. This approach achieves near-complete code reuse while delivering desktop-class functionality.

## 7.4 UI/Backend Integration

### 7.4.1 API Communication Protocol

**Base Configuration:**

```
Protocol: HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
Base URL: https://api.newnov6.com
API Version: /api/v1/
Request Format: JSON
Response Format: JSON
Authentication: Bearer JWT in Authorization header
```

**Standard Request Headers:**

```http
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json
X-Request-ID: req_abc123xyz789
User-Agent: NewNov6-Web/1.0.0 (Platform: Web)
```

**API Endpoint Structure:**

```
Authentication:
POST   /api/v1/auth/signup           - User registration
POST   /api/v1/auth/login            - User authentication
POST   /api/v1/auth/logout           - Session termination

POST   /api/v1/auth/mfa/verify       - MFA verification

User Management:
GET    /api/v1/users/{user_id}                - Retrieve user profile
PATCH  /api/v1/users/{user_id}                - Update user profile
DELETE /api/v1/users/{user_id}                - Delete user account
GET    /api/v1/users/{user_id}/preferences    - Get preferences

AI Orchestration:
POST   /api/v1/ai/query                       - Submit AI query
```

**Standard Response Formats:**

**Success Response:**
```json
{

    "user_id": "auth0|507f1f77bcf86cd799439011",
```

```json
{

    }
  },
```

```
Authentication Errors: UNAUTHORIZED, TOKEN_EXPIRED, INVALID_CREDENTIALS
Authorization Errors: FORBIDDEN, INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS

Resource Errors: NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, RESOURCE_LOCKED
Rate Limiting: RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, QUOTA_EXCEEDED
Server Errors: INTERNAL_ERROR, SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE
```

### 7.4.2 Authentication Flow

The UI implements OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow with Auth0 as the identity provider:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Client as UI Client
    participant Auth0
    participant Backend as API Backend
    participant Redis as Redis Cache

    User->>Client: Click "Log In"
    Client->>Auth0: Redirect to /authorize<br/>(client_id, redirect_uri, scope)
    Auth0->>User: Present login page
    User->>Auth0: Enter credentials
    Auth0->>User: MFA challenge (if enabled)
    User->>Auth0: Submit MFA code
    Auth0->>Client: Redirect with authorization code
    Client->>Auth0: POST /oauth/token<br/>(code, client_id, client_secret)
    Auth0->>Client: Return tokens<br/>(access_token, refresh_token, id_token)
    Client->>Client: Store tokens securely<br/>(httpOnly cookie or secure storage)
    Client->>Backend: API request with<br/>Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
    Backend->>Redis: Verify token in cache
    Redis->>Backend: Token valid
    Backend->>Client: Protected resource
    Client->>User: Display content

    Note over Client,Backend: Token Refresh Flow
    Client->>Client: Detect token expiration<br/>(5 minutes before expiry)
    Client->>Auth0: POST /oauth/token<br/>(grant_type=refresh_token)
    Auth0->>Client: New access token
    Client->>Client: Update stored token
    Client->>Backend: Retry failed request
```

**Token Storage by Platform:**

- **Web**: httpOnly cookies with Secure and SameSite=Lax flags (XSS protection)
- **React Native**: react-native-keychain (iOS Keychain, Android Keystore)
- **Native iOS**: iOS Keychain Services API
- **Native Android**: Android Keystore System with AES encryption
- **Electron**: electron-store with native credential storage
- **macOS**: macOS Keychain Services

**Token Lifecycle:**
- Access Token TTL: 15-60 minutes (configurable per environment)
- Refresh Token TTL: 30 days
- Automatic refresh: Triggered 5 minutes before access token expiration
- Session timeout: 12 hours of inactivity triggers re-authentication

### 7.4.3 File Upload Pattern

The direct-to-S3 upload pattern minimizes backend load and maximizes upload performance:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant UI as UI Client
    participant Backend as API Backend
    participant S3 as AWS S3
    participant CloudFront
    participant MongoDB

    User->>UI: Select file for upload
    UI->>UI: Client-side validation<br/>(type, size)
    UI->>Backend: POST /api/v1/files/request-upload<br/>{filename, content_type, size_bytes}
    Backend->>S3: Generate pre-signed PUT URL<br/>(15-minute expiry)
    Backend->>MongoDB: Create file record<br/>(status: pending)
    Backend->>UI: Return {upload_url, file_id, s3_key}
    UI->>UI: Display upload progress UI
    UI->>S3: PUT file to pre-signed URL<br/>(direct upload, bypass backend)
    S3->>UI: Upload complete (HTTP 200)
    UI->>Backend: POST /api/v1/files/confirm-upload<br/>{file_id, s3_key}
    Backend->>S3: Verify object exists (HEAD request)
    S3->>Backend: Object metadata
    Backend->>MongoDB: Update file record<br/>(status: completed)
    Backend->>UI: Upload confirmed
    UI->>User: Display success message

    Note over User,CloudFront: File Download Flow
    User->>UI: Click download button
    UI->>Backend: GET /api/v1/files/{file_id}
    Backend->>MongoDB: Retrieve file metadata
    Backend->>CloudFront: Generate signed URL<br/>(1-hour expiry)
    Backend->>UI: Return {cdn_url}
    UI->>CloudFront: GET file from CDN
    CloudFront->>S3: Fetch from origin (if not cached)
    CloudFront->>UI: Stream file
    UI->>User: Download file
```

**Upload Progress Tracking:**

The UI implements client-side progress tracking using XMLHttpRequest or Fetch API progress events:

```typescript
// Progress tracking implementation approach
const uploadFile = async (file: File, uploadUrl: string) => {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const xhr = new XMLHttpRequest();
    
    xhr.upload.addEventListener('progress', (event) => {
      if (event.lengthComputable) {
        const percentComplete = (event.loaded / event.total) * 100;
        updateProgressUI(percentComplete);
      }
    });
    
    xhr.addEventListener('load', () => {
      if (xhr.status === 200) resolve(xhr.response);
      else reject(new Error('Upload failed'));
    });
    
    xhr.open('PUT', uploadUrl);
    xhr.setRequestHeader('Content-Type', file.type);
    xhr.send(file);
  });
};
```

**Error Handling:**
- Upload timeout: 5 minutes for files under 100MB, scaled for larger files
- Network interruption: Retry with exponential backoff (3 attempts)
- Pre-signed URL expiration: Request new URL and restart upload
- File validation failure: Display specific error message with allowed formats

### 7.4.4 Rate Limiting

The UI must handle and communicate rate limits to users:

**Rate Limit Configuration:**

```
Endpoint Category       | Requests | Time Window | Scope
------------------------|----------|-------------|----------
General API             | 60       | 1 minute    | Per user
Authentication          | 5        | 5 minutes   | Per IP
AI Query Submission     | 10-100   | 1 hour      | Per user (tier-based)
File Upload Request     | 20       | 1 hour      | Per user
File Upload Confirm     | 25       | 1 hour      | Per user
Admin Operations        | 100      | 1 minute    | Per admin user
```

**Rate Limit Response Headers:**

```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1699282860
Retry-After: 60
```

**UI Rate Limit Handling:**

1. **Proactive Display**: Show remaining quota in UI (e.g., "8 AI queries remaining this hour")
2. **Warning Threshold**: Warn user when 80% of quota consumed
3. **Graceful Degradation**: Disable submit button when quota exhausted
4. **Countdown Timer**: Display time until quota reset (from X-RateLimit-Reset header)
5. **Client-Side Throttling**: Queue requests to prevent immediate rate limit breaches
6. **User Education**: Tooltip explaining rate limits and how to increase quota

**Rate Limit Error Display:**

```
User-Friendly Message:
"You've reached your hourly limit for AI queries. Your quota will reset in 
42 minutes. Consider upgrading to Power User for higher limits."

Technical Details (collapsible):
- Current tier: Standard User
- Limit: 10 queries/hour
- Reset time: 2024-11-06 16:30:00 UTC
- Upgrade options: [View Plans]
```

## 7.5 Data Models and Schemas

### 7.5.1 User Profile Schema

```typescript
interface User {
  // Identity
  user_id: string;                    // Unique identifier from Auth0 (e.g., "auth0|507f1f77bcf86cd799439011")
  email: string;                      // User email address (unique, validated)
  email_verified: boolean;            // Email verification status
  
  // Profile Information
  name: string;                       // Full name
  avatar_url?: string;                // Profile picture URL (optional)
  phone_number?: string;              // Phone number (optional, E.164 format)
  phone_verified?: boolean;           // Phone verification status
  
  // Authorization
  roles: UserRole[];                  // Assigned roles
  permissions: Permission[];          // Granular permissions
  
  // User Preferences
  preferences: UserPreferences;
  
  // Metadata
  created_at: string;                 // ISO 8601 timestamp
  updated_at: string;                 // ISO 8601 timestamp
  last_login_at?: string;             // Last successful authentication
  
  // Account Status
  status: 'active' | 'suspended' | 'locked' | 'deleted';
  lockout_until?: string;             // Temporary lockout expiration
}

type UserRole = 'admin' | 'power_user' | 'standard_user' | 'read_only';

type Permission = 
  | 'users:read' | 'users:write' | 'users:delete'
  | 'ai:query' | 'ai:advanced_models' | 'ai:custom_models'
  | 'files:upload' | 'files:download' | 'files:delete' | 'files:share'
  | 'admin:users' | 'admin:config' | 'admin:audit' | 'admin:metrics';

interface UserPreferences {
  // Display
  theme: 'light' | 'dark' | 'auto';
  language: string;                   // ISO 639-1 code (e.g., "en", "es", "fr")
  
  // Notifications
  notifications_enabled: boolean;
  email_notifications: boolean;
  push_notifications: boolean;
  notification_frequency: 'immediate' | 'daily_digest' | 'weekly_digest';
  
  // AI Preferences
  default_ai_model?: string;          // e.g., "gpt-4-turbo-preview"
  ai_response_format?: 'concise' | 'detailed' | 'technical';
  
  // Accessibility
  reduced_motion: boolean;
  high_contrast: boolean;
  font_size_multiplier: number;       // 0.8 to 1.5
}
```

### 7.5.2 AI Conversation Schema

```typescript
interface AIConversation {
  // Identity
  conversation_id: string;            // Unique identifier (e.g., "conv_abc123xyz")
  user_id: string;                    // Owner user ID
  
  // Conversation Content
  title: string;                      // Auto-generated or user-defined
  messages: Message[];                // Ordered message array
  
  // AI Configuration
  llm_provider: 'openai' | 'anthropic' | 'custom';
  model: string;                      // e.g., "gpt-4-turbo-preview", "claude-3-opus"
  temperature?: number;               // 0.0 to 2.0 (default 0.7)
  max_tokens?: number;                // Response length limit
  
  // RAG Configuration (if applicable)
  rag_enabled: boolean;
  source_documents?: string[];        // File IDs used for RAG
  
  // Usage Metrics
  total_tokens: number;               // Cumulative token usage
  estimated_cost: number;             // USD cost estimate
  
  // Metadata
  created_at: string;                 // ISO 8601 timestamp
  updated_at: string;                 // Last message timestamp
  archived: boolean;
  tags?: string[];                    // User-defined tags
}

interface Message {
  message_id: string;                 // Unique message identifier
  role: 'user' | 'assistant' | 'system';
  content: string;                    // Message text (supports markdown)
  timestamp: string;                  // ISO 8601 timestamp
  
  // AI Response Metadata (for assistant messages)
  model?: string;                     // Model that generated response
  tokens?: number;                    // Token count for this message
  finish_reason?: 'stop' | 'length' | 'content_filter';
  
  // RAG Metadata (if applicable)
  citations?: Citation[];             // Source document references
}

interface Citation {
  source_document_id: string;

}
```

### 7.5.3 File Metadata Schema

```typescript
interface FileMetadata {
  // Identity
  file_id: string;                    // Unique identifier (e.g., "file_abc123xyz")
  user_id: string;                    // Owner user ID
  
  // File Information
  filename: string;                   // Original filename with extension
  content_type: string;               // MIME type (e.g., "image/jpeg", "application/pdf")
  size_bytes: number;                 // File size in bytes
  checksum: string;                   // SHA-256 hash for integrity verification
  
  // Storage Location
  s3_bucket: string;                  // S3 bucket name
  s3_key: string;                     // S3 object key
  s3_version_id?: string;             // S3 version ID (if versioning enabled)
  
  // Access Control
  is_public: boolean;                 // Public accessibility
  cdn_url?: string;                   // CloudFront URL (if public)
  sharing_enabled: boolean;
  shared_with?: string[];             // User IDs with access
  
  // File Processing
  processing_status: 'pending' | 'processing' | 'completed' | 'failed';
  thumbnail_url?: string;             // Thumbnail for images/videos
  extracted_text?: string;            // OCR or text extraction result
  
  // Metadata
  created_at: string;                 // Upload timestamp
  updated_at: string;                 // Last modification
  expires_at?: string;                // Automatic deletion timestamp (optional)
  
  // User-Defined Metadata
  tags?: string[];
  description?: string;
  folder_path?: string;               // Hierarchical organization
}
```

### 7.5.4 API Response Schema

```typescript
interface APIResponse<T> {
  status: 'success' | 'error';
  data?: T;                           // Present on success
  error?: APIError;                   // Present on error
  metadata: ResponseMetadata;
}

interface APIError {
  code: ErrorCode;
  message: string;                    // User-friendly error message
  details?: Record<string, any>;      // Additional context
  stack_trace?: string;               // Only in development environment
}

type ErrorCode =
  // Authentication
  | 'UNAUTHORIZED' | 'TOKEN_EXPIRED' | 'INVALID_CREDENTIALS' | 'MFA_REQUIRED'
  // Authorization
  | 'FORBIDDEN' | 'INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS' | 'RESOURCE_FORBIDDEN'
  // Validation
  | 'VALIDATION_ERROR' | 'INVALID_INPUT' | 'MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD'
  // Resources
  | 'NOT_FOUND' | 'CONFLICT' | 'RESOURCE_LOCKED' | 'RESOURCE_DELETED'
  // Rate Limiting
  | 'RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED' | 'QUOTA_EXCEEDED' | 'CONCURRENT_REQUEST_LIMIT'
  // Server
  | 'INTERNAL_ERROR' | 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE' | 'GATEWAY_TIMEOUT'
  | 'DATABASE_ERROR' | 'EXTERNAL_SERVICE_ERROR';

interface ResponseMetadata {
  timestamp: string;                  // ISO 8601 timestamp
  request_id: string;                 // Unique request identifier for tracing
  version: string;                    // API version (e.g., "v1")
  duration_ms?: number;               // Request processing time
}

// Pagination Envelope
interface PaginatedResponse<T> extends APIResponse<T[]> {
  pagination: {
    total_count: number;              // Total items across all pages
    page: number;                     // Current page (1-indexed)
    page_size: number;                // Items per page
    total_pages: number;              // Total page count
    has_next: boolean;
    has_previous: boolean;
    next_page?: number;
    previous_page?: number;
  };
}
```

### 7.5.5 Authentication Token Schema

```typescript
interface AuthTokens {
  access_token: string;               // JWT access token
  refresh_token: string;              // Refresh token (opaque)
  id_token: string;                   // OpenID Connect ID token
  token_type: 'Bearer';
  expires_in: number;                 // Seconds until expiration
  scope: string;                      // Space-separated scope list
}

// Decoded JWT Access Token Payload
interface JWTPayload {
  // Standard Claims
  iss: string;                        // Issuer (Auth0 tenant URL)
  sub: string;                        // Subject (user_id)
  aud: string[];                      // Audience (API identifier)
  iat: number;                        // Issued at (Unix timestamp)
  exp: number;                        // Expiration (Unix timestamp)
  azp: string;                        // Authorized party (client_id)
  scope: string;                      // Space-separated permissions
  
  // Custom Claims
  email: string;
  email_verified: boolean;
  name: string;
  roles: UserRole[];
  permissions: Permission[];
  
  // Metadata
  'https://newnov6.com/app_metadata': {
    user_tier: 'free' | 'standard' | 'premium' | 'enterprise';
    feature_flags: string[];
  };
}
```

## 7.6 Screen Specifications

### 7.6.1 Authentication Screens

#### 7.6.1.1 Login Screen

**Screen Purpose:** Primary entry point for user authentication

**UI Components:**
- Application logo and tagline
- Email input field (type="email", autocomplete="username")
- Password input field (type="password", autocomplete="current-password")
- "Remember me" checkbox (stores refresh token with extended TTL)
- "Forgot password?" link (navigates to password reset flow)
- "Log in" primary button (submits authentication request)
- Horizontal divider with "OR" text
- Social authentication buttons:
  - "Continue with Google" (branded button with Google logo)
  - "Continue with GitHub" (branded button with GitHub logo)
  - "Continue with Microsoft" (branded button with Microsoft logo)
- "Don't have an account? Sign up" link

**Validation Rules:**
- Email: Valid email format, required
- Password: Minimum 1 character (actual validation server-side), required
- Submit button disabled until both fields populated

**Success Flow:**
1. Submit credentials to Auth0
2. Receive authorization code
3. Exchange for tokens
4. Store tokens securely
5. Redirect to intended destination or dashboard
6. Display welcome toast notification

**Error Handling:**
- Invalid credentials: "Email or password is incorrect"
- Account locked: "Your account has been locked due to too many failed login attempts. Please reset your password or contact support."
- MFA required: Redirect to MFA challenge screen
- Network error: "Unable to connect. Please check your internet connection and try again."

#### 7.6.1.2 Signup/Registration Screen

**Screen Purpose:** New user account creation

**UI Components:**
- "Create your account" heading
- Full name input field (autocomplete="name")
- Email address input field (autocomplete="email")
- Password input field with visibility toggle (autocomplete="new-password")
- Password strength indicator:
  - Visual strength bar (red → yellow → green)
  - Text indicator ("Weak", "Fair", "Strong")
  - Requirements checklist:
    - ✓ At least 8 characters
    - ✓ Contains uppercase letter
    - ✓ Contains lowercase letter
    - ✓ Contains number
    - ✓ Contains special character
- Confirm password input field
- Terms of service checkbox with inline link
- Privacy policy checkbox with inline link
- "Create account" primary button
- "Already have an account? Log in" link

**Validation Rules:**
- Name: Required, 2-100 characters
- Email: Valid format, unique (checked server-side), required
- Password: Meets strength requirements, required
- Confirm password: Matches password field
- Both checkboxes must be checked

**Success Flow:**
1. Submit registration data to Auth0
2. Account created
3. Email verification sent
4. Redirect to dashboard with "Please verify your email" banner
5. Display success message

**Error Handling:**
- Email already exists: "An account with this email already exists. Would you like to log in instead?"
- Weak password: Inline error with specific requirements not met
- Terms not accepted: "You must accept the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy to continue"

#### 7.6.1.3 Multi-Factor Authentication Setup Screen

**Screen Purpose:** Configure MFA methods for account security

**UI Components:**
- "Secure your account" heading
- MFA method selection tabs:
  - **Authenticator App** (recommended)
  - **SMS**
  - **Email**
- Authenticator App tab content:
  - QR code for scanning (generated by Auth0)
  - Manual entry code (for apps that don't support QR)
  - Instructions: "Scan this QR code with your authenticator app"
  - Supported apps list: Google Authenticator, Authy, Microsoft Authenticator
  - 6-digit verification code input
  - "Verify and activate" button
- Backup codes section:
  - "Save your backup codes" warning
  - 10 one-time-use backup codes displayed
  - "Download codes" button
  - "Copy codes" button
  - "I've saved my codes" checkbox
- "Skip for now" secondary button
- "Continue" primary button (enabled after verification)

**Success Flow:**
1. User scans QR code
2. Enters verification code
3. Code validated by Auth0
4. Backup codes generated and displayed
5. User confirms codes saved
6. MFA activated on account
7. Redirect to dashboard with success message

#### 7.6.1.4 MFA Challenge Screen

**Screen Purpose:** Authenticate user with second factor

**UI Components:**
- "Verify your identity" heading
- User email display (partially masked: "u***@example.com")
- 6-digit code input (auto-focus, numeric keyboard on mobile)
- "Remember this device for 30 days" checkbox
- "Verify" primary button
- "Use a different method" dropdown:
  - SMS to phone ending in ***1234
  - Email to u***@example.com
  - Use backup code
- "Cancel and log out" secondary button
- Resend code timer (30-second countdown)

**Validation Rules:**
- Code: Exactly 6 digits, required
- 3 failed attempts trigger account lockout

**Success Flow:**
1. User enters MFA code
2. Code validated by Auth0
3. MFA successful
4. Tokens issued
5. Redirect to intended destination

**Error Handling:**
- Invalid code: "Invalid verification code. Please try again."
- Expired code: "This code has expired. Request a new code."
- Too many attempts: "Too many failed attempts. Your account has been locked for 15 minutes."
